blockingFindings.title: Staged Mutations Can Complete As Passing Evidence
blockingFindings.issue: The repository mutation guard compares `git write-tree` before and after the regression run, but `write-tree` only reflects the index. A regression command can modify a tracked file and then `git add` it; after the run, `git diff --no-ext-diff --binary HEAD` in `finalRegressionWorktreeFingerprint` is unchanged from the pre-run staged diff, and `write-tree` can also match the pre-run index tree if the same staged content was already present. That allows a command that mutates the working tree during execution to be accepted as completed pass evidence.
blockingFindings.suggestion: In `RunFinalRegressionCommand.execute`, bind and compare both staged and working-tree content separately before and after the run, for example by hashing `git diff --cached --binary HEAD` and `git diff --binary` or by making `finalRegressionWorktreeFingerprint` include index and unstaged fingerprints independently. Add an R2 test where a passing command modifies a tracked file and stages it before exiting.
blockingFindings.rationale: R2 requires acceptance to validate execution binding against the current repository state and reject stale or mutated execution evidence. A passing command that can alter tracked source state and still complete as report-ready evidence violates that mandatory acceptance requirement.
